newsitem.title: DUBAI: Unclear rules hampering investment - Iran official.
newsitem.headline: Unclear rules hampering investment - Iran official.

text.p: The lack of clear guidelines on currency exchange is hampering foreign investment in Iran's free trade zones, a senior official said in remarks published on Tuesday.

"The lack of guidelines on money, banking and rates of exchange has caused us to be unable to give suitable answers to people seeking to invest, particularly foreigners," said Mehdi Lahuti, director of investment promotion at the Chahbahar free trade zone, in remarks quoted by the newspaper Iran.
"The central bank has not said its final word on the rate of exchange and only says foreign banks can open branches (in the zones)," Lahuti was quoted as saying by the daily Resalat.
Iranian central bank Governor Mohsen Nourbakhsh said last week the government planned to allow foreign banks to establish branches in the zones.

Iran has two official foreign exchange rates which differ significantly from the rate used on the black market. A rate of 3,000 rials to the dollar is used for most export transactions while a rate of 1,750 rials to the dollar is followed for certain state budget accounts.

Th rate used in the black market inside Iran and in exchange houses abroad is about 4,700 rials to the dollar. Many Iranians have to buy hard cash at this rate as state banks only supply limited amounts of foreign currency to travellers and business executives at the official rate.
Iran has stringent rules on sending hard currency abroad. The rules have hampered foreign investment in the country because of difficulties in repatriating profits.
Iran set up free trade zones on 1989 on Kish and Qeshm islands in the Gulf and in the southeastern port of Chahbahar.
